fdroid:com.l5rcm.companion.description:
A companion app for L5RCM, the Legend of the Five Rings 4th Edition character
manager. It is a play-at-the-table tool for players, not a character builder:
advancement and editing are out of scope.

fdroid:eu.lapotre.prochaintrain.name: Prochain train
fdroid:eu.lapotre.prochaintrain.summary: Real-time departures at the Paris-region stops you follow (French only)
fdroid:eu.lapotre.prochaintrain.description:
Prochain train shows the next departures (train, RER, metro, tram, bus) at the Île-de-France (Paris region) stops of your choice, in real time, using data from Île-de-France Mobilités.
 The app is in French only , as it covers the Paris region only.
 Features 
 My places : for each place you follow, the next departures grouped by line and destination, with the line badge in its official colors, the waiting time ("3 min, then 11 · 19") and the platform when it is announced.
 Add a place : search by station, stop or town name, or list the stops around you.
 Lines and directions : pick the lines to follow and, for each one, a direction. Only the trips that later stop at the chosen station are shown (for example, at Gare du Nord, only the line H trains that stop at Écouen - Ézanville).
 Light on resources 
 No external library, no background service, no tracker: the app weighs less than 100 KB.
 Departures never refresh on their own: once when the app opens, then when you ask. Waiting times are recomputed on screen, without a new request.
 Your location is only requested when you tap "Arrêts autour de moi" (stops around me), never in the background.
 Requirement : a free PRIM API key, to create on https://prim.iledefrance-mobilites.fr. The first screen explains how to get it.
 The data comes from Île-de-France Mobilités (PRIM "Prochains passages" API and open data) and remains subject to their terms of use.

firefox-addons:3056015.name: SpotCheck: Accessibility Toolkit
firefox-addons:3056015.summary: Toggle any of the tests to spot check common accessibility issues. Each one links to its related WCAG 2.2 success criteria.
firefox-addons:3056015.description:
A Chrome DevTools collection of tests that allow you to spot-check common accessibility issues directly in the browser. Each one links to its related WCAG 2.2 success criteria.
Available tools:
• Landmark Visualizer
Outlines every ARIA and HTML landmark region and flags ones missing an accessible name or duplicated.
• Link Accessibility Auditor
Checks every link for a real accessible name and flags generic text like “click here”.
• Heading Validator
Walks the heading outline in document order and flags any level that skips ahead.
• List Identifier
Flags empty lists, malformed markup, and list items that aren’t inside a list at all.
• Tab Order Visualizer
Numbers every focusable element in tab order and flags positive tabindex values.
• Text Contrast Checker
Measures text contrast against its effective background and flags anything below WCAG AA minimum.
• Alt Text Checker
Checks every image for alt text and flags the ones missing it or marked incorrectly.
• Input Label Checker
Outlines every input, select, and textarea on the page, then labels each one with how it gets its accessible name.
• Target Size Checker
Run this on any page to measure every clickable target, flag the ones under 24 by 24 CSS pixels, and show which ones clear the 44 by 44 enhanced threshold.
• Table Name Checker
Outlines every semantic table on the page, and shows where its accessible name comes from.
How to open your browser's DevTools
Open DevTools with Keyboard Shortcut
- Windows/Linux: Press F12 or Ctrl + Shift + I
- macOS: Press Cmd + Option + I
Open DevTools from Browser Menu
Browser menu --> More tools --> Developer tools
- Click the browser’s menu icon (⋮ or ☰)
- Select "More tools"
- Choose "Developer tools"
Open DevTools by Inspecting an Element
- Right‑click any part of the webpage to open the menu
- Select "Inspect" or "Inspect element" from the menu
Open DevTools via Command Menu : Chrome / Edge
- Press Ctrl + Shift + P (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + Shift + P (macOS)
- Type “DevTools” or the panel name (e.g., “Elements”, “Console”)

- Added the ability to access the tools from the Browser Extension Bar : 09/12/2026
- Added the Target Size Checker : 08/21/2026

Global Search: Effortlessly search for classes, components, flows, and metadata within your Salesforce org. Use advanced filters (Code, UI, Security, Flow) to find exactly what you need in seconds.
Log Analysis: Quickly search, filter, and review Salesforce debug logs. A powerful tool for developers and admins to identify issues and gain insights faster with a streamlined interface.
Permission Analyzer: Perform deep-dive analysis of user permissions. Understand exactly what access a user has and identify the overlapping contributions of Profiles and Permission Sets.
Profile & Permission Set Comparison: Compare profiles and permission sets side-by-side to identify differences and ensure consistent security settings across your Salesforce org.
Dev Library (Snippet Manager): Build your own repository of frequently used code snippets, SOQL queries, and configurations. Store, reuse, and share your knowledge to boost development speed.
CSV Export & Quick Shortcuts: Easily export comparison results and analysis data into CSV files. Navigate instantly to key Salesforce setup pages using built-in high-productivity shortcuts.
Simplify your Salesforce management with this powerful and easy-to-use extension, designed for both admins and developers looking to enhance their productivity.

firefox-addons:852819.description:
Automatically changes theme according to customizable schedule.
 Schedule up to two themes at a time.
 Any installed theme can be scheduled.
 Note 1: Extension checks if theme should be changed every 5 minutes. So if a theme is scheduled to change at 08:00, it will change between 08:00 and 08:05 depending on when the timer started.
 Note 2: No updates or added features are planned.
 Note 3: If you encounter a bug or want to request a feature, please file an issue here .
